Measured basis on rc3 5071f388 (4 held-out 4 KiB chunks of the Loghub OpenSSH sample, 64 KiB of earlier chunks as prior, rc3 binary only, marginal size = size(-x -n prior||file) - size(-x -n prior)): untrained -x 1,490 B; rc3 trained profile at hc (zstd 19 + dictionary) 1,031 B; the same profile at -x 1,342 B and at ratio 1,769 B (the strong modes get nothing from a profile: dictionaries reach zstd/Brotli/LZ4 leaves only, SPEC 'CMPR ... reserved; no writer yet'); CM warmed on the prior 336 B. Seven-set table in reviews/R11.md. Work: (1) KPR1 pack file (versioned, sectioned, CRC-32C, identified by SHA-256 of its body written from FIPS 180-4 as original code; priming text section + type key + parent id + settings); (2) codec 39 = codec-7 model 2/3 stream whose model first codes the pack's priming text without output, table size fixed by the pack so a primed model can be snapshotted and reused across files in one process; frame names the pack by hash (header flag + id, full hash optional); (3) decode without the pack, or with a damaged/other pack, stops before any block with a new error naming the hash (never wrong bytes: pack hash checked on load, block checksum after); (4) --embed: the pack travels inside the frame as an extension section so the file is self-contained; (5) encoder keeps the primed coding only when smaller than the rc3 coding of the block; (6) tests, fuzz of the pack parser, SPEC. Default OFF: without --prior frames are byte-identical to rc3. Measure: 7 held-out small-file sets (logs, C, HTML, CSV per country, wiki articles) against untrained -x/ratio/hc and rc3 profiles; encode/decode time and RSS with and without the snapshot cache. NOT covered: the automatic store that builds packs (my prior-store-autolearn); compiled-in per-kind priors and model 4 of the unmerged rc3w3 prior lane (static tables from public data); #40 (codec-25 parts primed on a prefix of the SAME block, for threads); #15 (native LZ prefix dictionary); #32/#51 (encoder-only experience store, frames unmarked); priming of BWT/LZMA2/KLZMA (my prior-pack-lz).

title: Self-accumulating prior store (opt-in --priors DIR / KOLMO_PRIORS): packs per detected file type are built automatically from the files Kolmo compresses, so the k-th file of a type is smaller than the first; content-addressed, portable, versioned, with rollback
scope: The store and portability half of cross-file learning (no training step, sizes change). (1) Type key from the bytes only (rc3's profile key: normalised first line / binary head, plus text-binary class); (2) after each compress the store keeps a bounded sample of the file per key in a checksummed append-only journal; at fixed byte thresholds (deterministic, not time- or thread-dependent) it builds generation g+1 of the key's pack with Kolmo's own selector (most-reused segments under a byte budget; original code, no ZDICT); (3) packs are immutable files named by their SHA-256, written atomically (temp + rename); a frame names the exact pack it used, so output = f(input, parameters, pack) and is reproducible with the same pack; the encoder reads one snapshot of the store per call; (4) decoder resolves the pack by hash from the store path(s) or an explicit --prior FILE; missing/corrupt pack -> error naming the hash and how to import it, never wrong bytes; (5) portability: kolmo prior export FRAMES.. (the packs those frames need), import, list, verify, pin/rollback KEY GEN, forget; nothing is ever deleted implicitly; a damaged journal or pack is quarantined and the encoder falls back to the rc3 coding (valid frame, no prior); (6) --embed-prior first|always for self-contained frames; (7) honest costs reported: packs hold samples of earlier files (privacy: opt-in, never on by default, export is explicit), files written with a store need the pack to decode. Measure: learning curves (size of the k-th file against k) on 7 small-file sets in arrival order against untrained rc3 and against an rc3 profile trained once on the first half; store size; corruption/rollback/missing-pack tests; byte-identical frames to rc3 when the option is off. Uses codec 39 of my cm-prior-pack as the first consumer. NOT covered: #32/#51/#53/#54 (R10's encoder-side experience store: outcomes and plans only, frames unmarked and decodable without it - this claim is the complement, where the decoder needs the state); kolmo train/-P profiles themselves; the pack consumers for LZ/LZMA (my prior-pack-lz) and transforms (my prior-struct-templates).

title: Experience store learns coder parameters that today's per-file search never tries: LZMA2 lc/lp/pb per data kind (measured -0.27% to -0.40% on three Silesia files, different winner on each) and CM learning settings beyond the four race presets and for streams above 16 MiB; no format change
scope: Encoder parameter choice only, among values rc3 decoders already read (LZMA2 properties in the codec-6 payload header, set today only through the hidden level>=100 hook of codecs/lzma.c; the two CM learning-setting bytes of tuned codec-7 streams). The per-file search is too slow (a full LZMA2 coding per candidate; docs/TWOPASS.md 2a: 49 CM codings), so the store of #32 spreads it over files: each call may code ONE extra candidate (a neighbour of the kind's current champion) on a 256 KiB-1 MiB slice, records slice sizes, and a champion replaces the default for that kind only after it beat it on k files with a margin; periodic re-check against the default. Measured on rc3 (-m ratio -l (lc+1)*100+lp*10+pb, exact sizes, round trips ok, results/R10-work/lclppb_table.md, 15 settings x 3 files): sao best 0/0/2 2,176,126 vs default 2,184,759 (-0.40%); x-ray best 1/0/0 3,606,803 vs 3,616,667 (-0.27%); ooffice best 4/0/2 2,085,304 vs 2,091,923 (-0.32%); a wrong setting costs up to +1.47%, so the choice must be per kind and verified. Small, recorded so nobody builds it blind; opt-in with --learn. NOT covered: LZMA2 presets/match finder or MT (#6), KLZMA (#43), CM models or priors (#2, #19, #56, #57: R11's prior packs change the bytes a decoder needs; this changes none), the race itself (kept as the fallback), any default change.
